newsitem.title: POLAND: ISUZU LAUNCHES POLISH PLANT CONSTRUCTION.
newsitem.headline: ISUZU LAUNCHES POLISH PLANT CONSTRUCTION.

text.p: Japan's Isuzu Motors Ltd on Wednesday launched the construction of a 300 million mark plant in southern Poland to manufacture diesel engines, the biggest Japanese investment in Poland so far.

"The fact that the Japanese firm located a diesel engine factory in Poland can be a signal that we evaluate the Polish economy and its prospects well," Isuzu Motors' president Kazuhira Seki said after a groundbreaking ceremony.

Isuzu earlier announced that it planned to start production by mid-1999 with an annual output of 200,000 engines in 1999, and 300,000 in the year 2000. It said the some of the engines would be exported to the European Union.
The engines are also likely to be used for Opel passenger cars, made by General Motors' German subsidiary Adam Opel AG, which is building a car assembly plant nearby.
The Isuzu plant will be located in a special economic zone near the southern industrial city of Tychy.
Investors' in Poland's economic zones are exempted from the corporate tax, now at 38 percent, for 10 years and are entitled to a 50 percent reduction of the tax in the next 10 years.
